boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named, map-listed Kettering College spaces that support study, student services, meals, residence life, and health-professions learning.

cards.title: Use the Library’s research stations
cards.subtitle: Learning Commons, Boonshoft building
cards.notes: Bring a research question or class task; library computers provide course software, printing, OhioLINK access, and health-sciences databases.
cards.short_summary: A campus research base with library computers and OhioLINK access.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College locates the Library in the Learning Commons on the Boonshoft main level and lists computers, printing, OhioLINK, and databases there.
cards.source_title: Where Are Campus Computers Available? | Kettering College
cards.access_notes: Campus library services are intended for Kettering College students, faculty, and staff; check the library page for current hours.

cards.title: Reserve a group-study room
cards.subtitle: Lower level of the Learning Commons
cards.notes: Use SmartWay to reserve a room before meeting. If arriving without a booking, check the panel and respect an existing reservation.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms for collaborative study in the Learning Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: The College Library states that group study rooms are on the Learning Commons lower level and may be reserved through SmartWay.
cards.access_notes: Reservations use the SmartWay system; the library notes that unreserved use is possible but reservations should be honored.

cards.title: Meet in Polen Plaza
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Map, between the Boonshoft and Polen areas
cards.notes: Use this named common area as a clear on-campus meeting point before heading to nearby library, classroom, or café spaces.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed common area anchoring the college’s main campus circulation.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College’s Main Campus Map labels Polen Plaza as a common area.
cards.access_notes: Located on the Kettering College main campus; follow campus access and safety guidance.

cards.title: Plan a café stop between classes
cards.subtitle: Ground level, Boonshoft building
cards.notes: Use the campus map to find the café on the ground level; confirm offerings and payment options with the college before relying on it.
cards.short_summary: A named café shown beside the Learning Commons on the campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College’s Main Campus Map labels Anna May Café on the Boonshoft ground level.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current service and payment details directly with the college.

cards.title: Locate the campus cafeteria
cards.subtitle: Ground level, Boonshoft building
cards.notes: Use the map-listed cafeteria as a practical on-campus meal location; check current service, payment, and any student-account policies before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining location marked on the Boonshoft ground level.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College’s Main Campus Map labels a Cafeteria on the Boonshoft ground level.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current service and payment details directly with the college.

cards.entity_name: Kettering College Interprofessional Education Simulation Center
cards.title: See interprofessional practice in action
cards.subtitle: Ground level, Boonshoft building
cards.notes: For an approved course activity, prepare to work through simulated patient scenarios with an interdisciplinary team in a safe practice setting.
cards.short_summary: A simulation facility for collaborative healthcare training.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College describes the IPE Simulation Center as a healthcare training facility for interprofessional simulation and collaboration.
cards.access_notes: Normal operation is weekdays; after-hours or weekend access requires advance approval, and use is limited to approved programs.

cards.title: Find the Auditorium for campus programs
cards.subtitle: First level, Boonshoft building
cards.notes: Use the map-listed Auditorium as your navigation point when a college program names this venue; verify the event’s entry details in advance.
cards.short_summary: A named first-level campus venue on the official map.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College’s Main Campus Map labels an Auditorium on the Boonshoft first level.
cards.access_notes: Access depends on the scheduled college event or program.

cards.title: Connect with Student Success
cards.subtitle: First level, Boonshoft building
cards.notes: Start here when you need learning-strategy support, tutoring, group review, coaching, testing, or disability-services direction.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed support destination connected to academic success services.
cards.evidence_claim: The campus map labels Student Success / Title IX, and the academic bulletin lists tutoring, group review, coaching, testing, and disability services.
cards.access_notes: The office is mapped on the Boonshoft first level; contact the college for appointments or current availability.

cards.title: Know the Residence Hall connection
cards.subtitle: Kettering College main campus
cards.notes: If eligible for housing, use the Residence Hall page to review requirements and application steps before making move-in or lease plans.
cards.short_summary: College housing with social and spiritual programming for residents.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College states that its Residence Hall provides student housing and promotes social and spiritual opportunities for residents.
cards.access_notes: Housing has eligibility criteria, an application process, and an academic-year lease; see the college’s current residence-hall guidance.

cards.title: Use the lower-level student lounge
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Boonshoft building
cards.notes: Use this designated lounge as a between-class common area, and check the nearby printer status before planning a print-and-review stop.
cards.short_summary: A named student lounge area with access to a campus printer/copier.
cards.evidence_claim: The College Library identifies a printer/copier in the student lounge area on the lower level of the Boonshoft.
cards.access_notes: Printing and copying have per-page charges; follow campus access rules for the lounge.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten verified no-admission activities around Kettering College and the Dayton area.

cards.title: Browse Wright-Dunbar Visitor Center
cards.subtitle: Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park
cards.notes: Meet up to explore the visitor center’s Wright brothers and Paul Laurence Dunbar exhibits; it is free, though large groups need reservations.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost historic stop in the Wright-Dunbar neighborhood.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists the Wright-Dunbar Visitor Center as free and says reservations are required for school and large groups.
cards.source_title: Fees & Passes — Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Free; reservations required for school groups and large groups. Confirm operating hours before traveling.

cards.title: See the Wright Cycle Company
cards.subtitle: Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park
cards.notes: Take a small group through the restored Wright Cycle Company site and compare the workshop setting with the park’s aviation story.
cards.short_summary: Free access to a restored Wright brothers bicycle-shop site.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists the Wright Cycle Company as free and says reservations are required for school and large groups.
cards.source_title: Fees & Passes — Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Free; reservations required for school groups and large groups. Confirm operating hours before traveling.

cards.entity_name: Paul Laurence Dunbar House Historic Site
cards.title: Tour the Dunbar House
cards.subtitle: Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park
cards.notes: Plan a daytime visit with friends to learn about Paul Laurence Dunbar at his preserved Dayton home; tours have no admission fee.
cards.short_summary: A free historic-home visit focused on Dayton poet Paul Laurence Dunbar.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that there are no admission fees to visit the Paul Laurence Dunbar House Historic Site.
cards.source_title: Basic Information — Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: No admission fee; NPS lists tours Friday through Sunday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., with the final tour at 3:30 p.m. Confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Walk Huffman Prairie Flying Field
cards.subtitle: Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park
cards.notes: Use the field as a daylight walk-and-talk destination, then read the on-site interpretation about the Wright brothers’ flying experiments.
cards.short_summary: A free aviation-history landscape at the former Wright flying field.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists Huffman Prairie Flying Field as free and notes that large groups require reservations.
cards.source_title: Fees & Passes — Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Free; reservations required for school groups and large groups. Access is through Gate 16A off State Route 444.

cards.entity_name: Huffman Prairie Flying Field Interpretive Center
cards.title: Explore Huffman Prairie’s Interpretive Center
cards.subtitle: Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park
cards.notes: Pair the interpretive center with the nearby flying field for a no-cost, self-guided aviation-history outing during public operating times.
cards.short_summary: Free interpretation for the Wright brothers’ Huffman Prairie work.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists the Huffman Prairie Flying Field Interpretive Center as free and notes that large groups require reservations.
cards.source_title: Fees & Passes — Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Free; reservations required for school groups and large groups. Located on Wright-Patterson Air Force Base; confirm access details before visiting.

cards.title: Cool Off at Fairview Park
cards.subtitle: Fairview Park spray park, Dayton
cards.notes: Bring water and sunscreen for a daytime splash-pad meetup; the city identifies this as one of its free public spray-park locations.
cards.short_summary: A free public splash-pad option for a hot afternoon.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Dayton says its spray parks are free, need no registration, and lists Fairview Park at 2262 Elsmore Avenue.
cards.source_title: Maximize summer fun for free at Dayton’s splash pads
cards.access_notes: Free to the public with no registration; the city states spray parks run daily from noon to 8 p.m. during the summer season.

cards.title: Meet at Five Oaks Spray Park
cards.subtitle: Five Oaks Park spray park, Dayton
cards.notes: Make this a simple warm-weather group stop: bring a towel, use the public spray area, and follow the posted park rules.
cards.short_summary: A free public spray-pad hang in Five Oaks.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Dayton says its spray parks are free, need no registration, and lists Five Oaks Park at 329 Five Oaks Avenue.
cards.source_title: Maximize summer fun for free at Dayton’s splash pads
cards.access_notes: Free to the public with no registration; the city states spray parks run daily from noon to 8 p.m. during the summer season.

cards.title: Take a Splash Break at Mallory Park
cards.subtitle: Mallory Park spray park, Dayton
cards.notes: Coordinate a low-key daytime cool-down at this public spray park, then dry off and continue the outing elsewhere in the neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A free public splash-pad stop on Germantown Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Dayton says its spray parks are free, need no registration, and lists Mallory Park at 3037 Germantown Street.
cards.source_title: Maximize summer fun for free at Dayton’s splash pads
cards.access_notes: Free to the public with no registration; the city states spray parks run daily from noon to 8 p.m. during the summer season.

cards.title: Gather at McIntosh Park
cards.subtitle: McIntosh Park spray park, Dayton
cards.notes: Use the public spray area for a no-cost daytime meetup; bring what you need and respect the park’s posted rules and other visitors.
cards.short_summary: A free public splash-pad option near Riverview Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Dayton says its spray parks are free, need no registration, and lists McIntosh Park at 882 West Riverview Avenue.
cards.source_title: Maximize summer fun for free at Dayton’s splash pads
cards.access_notes: Free to the public with no registration; the city states spray parks run daily from noon to 8 p.m. during the summer season.

cards.title: Visit Stuart Patterson Spray Park
cards.subtitle: Stuart Patterson Park spray park, Dayton
cards.notes: Choose a daytime window for a casual splash-pad hang, and bring a towel and water for a comfortable no-purchase outing.
cards.short_summary: A free public splash-pad hang on Baltimore Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Dayton says its spray parks are free, need no registration, and lists Stuart Patterson Park at 238 Baltimore Street.
cards.source_title: Maximize summer fun for free at Dayton’s splash pads
cards.access_notes: Free to the public with no registration; the city states spray parks run daily from noon to 8 p.m. during the summer season.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on practical Kettering-area corridors, each with one documented activity or feature to orient an off-campus stop.

cards.title: Pause by the civic art and pond
cards.subtitle: Lincoln Park Boulevard corridor — 675 Lincoln Park Blvd.
cards.notes: Walk the park path, look for the civic-art installations, and pause by the fishing pond before continuing along Lincoln Park Boulevard.
cards.short_summary: A 14-acre civic park with a pond, public art, benches, and paths beside Fraze Pavilion.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Kettering lists civic art, a fishing pond, picnic tables/benches, and event space at Lincoln Park Civic Commons, 675 Lincoln Park Blvd.
cards.access_notes: Review the city page for current park information and events.

cards.title: Check the outdoor venue calendar
cards.subtitle: Lincoln Park Boulevard corridor — 695 Lincoln Park Blvd.
cards.notes: Use the official venue calendar to identify an all-ages performance, then confirm the event’s ticket and entry details before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A 4,300-seat outdoor entertainment venue in Lincoln Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Fraze Pavilion identifies itself as a 4,300-seat outdoor entertainment venue at 695 Lincoln Park Boulevard in Kettering.
cards.access_notes: Ticketing and entry rules vary by event; check the official event listing.

cards.title: Choose a swim, skate, or track session
cards.subtitle: Glengarry Drive corridor — 2900 Glengarry Dr.
cards.notes: Check the facility schedule, then pick one documented option—swimming, skating, fitness, or the walk/run track—for a planned activity stop.
cards.short_summary: A city recreation facility with aquatic, ice, gym, fitness, and track amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kettering Recreation Complex at 2900 Glengarry Drive includes swimming, skating, fitness and wellness facilities, a gymnasium, and a walk/run track.
cards.access_notes: The city posts facility and track hours; program availability can change.

cards.title: Look for the gallery and ceramics program
cards.subtitle: Olson Drive corridor — 2655 Olson Dr.
cards.notes: Check the gallery’s current exhibition details, then plan a visit around the arts centre’s documented ceramics studios and exhibition space.
cards.short_summary: A city arts centre housing Rosewood Gallery, studios, classes, and a ceramics program.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Kettering describes Rosewood Arts Centre at 2655 Olson Drive as home to Rosewood Gallery and a ceramics program with studios and classes.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current gallery hours and class or exhibition access with the arts centre.

cards.title: Walk the trail past the history features
cards.subtitle: Delco Park Drive corridor — 1700 Delco Park Dr.
cards.notes: Follow the bike/walking path and make time for the Kettering Veterans Memorial and Charles F. Kettering History Walk within the park.
cards.short_summary: A city park with a walking path, pond, memorial, and local-history walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Kettering lists a bike/walking path, fishing pier/pond, Kettering Veterans Memorial, and Charles F. Kettering History Walk at Delco Park.
cards.access_notes: City information lists the park’s hours as dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Bring a racquet or ball for the courts
cards.subtitle: East David Road corridor — 1030 E. David Rd.
cards.notes: Use the city amenity list to choose a court or field activity, and check shelter-reservation details if you are coordinating a group.
cards.short_summary: A 14.1-acre city park with tennis, basketball, ball fields, and picnic facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Kettering lists tennis courts, basketball courts, ball fields, soccer fields, grills, and a reservable shelter at Ernst Park.
cards.access_notes: Shelter reservations have seasonal availability; consult the city page before planning a group visit.

cards.title: Use the walking path and splash pad
cards.subtitle: Bigger Road corridor — 5073 Bigger Road
cards.notes: Plan a daylight park stop around the walking path or splash pad, and treat the first-come shelters as unreserved shared space.
cards.short_summary: A 15-acre park with a walking path, splash pad, courts, and non-reservable shelters.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Kettering lists a walking path, splash pad, basketball courts, tennis courts, and first-come shelters at J. F. Kennedy Park.
cards.access_notes: The city identifies the shelters as non-reservable and first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Try the trails and nature-themed play area
cards.subtitle: Peach Orchard Road corridor — 915 Peach Orchard Rd.
cards.notes: Walk the winding trails and view the Major Dominic Gentile historical displays; check park conditions before using the playground features.
cards.short_summary: A 19-acre nature-themed park with trails, historical displays, playground equipment, and a zipline.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Kettering lists winding walking trails, historical displays, a nature-themed playground, climbing tower, and 100-plus-foot zipline at Gentile Nature Park.
cards.access_notes: Review the city page for current site conditions and amenity information.

cards.title: See the preserved farmhouse and barn grounds
cards.subtitle: Bigger Road corridor — 5099 Bigger Road
cards.notes: Walk the public picnic areas when the grounds are not reserved, and look for the historic farmhouse, barn, garden patio, and gazebo.
cards.short_summary: A 15-acre historic farm site with a nineteenth-century farmhouse, barn, gazebo, and picnic areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Kettering identifies Polen Farm at 5099 Bigger Road as a 15-acre site with a 19th-century farmhouse and barn; picnic areas are public when not reserved.
cards.access_notes: The buildings and grounds may be reserved for private renters; check availability before visiting.

cards.title: Take the Adirondack Trail past historic features
cards.subtitle: South Patterson Boulevard corridor — Oakwood-Kettering
cards.notes: Use the park’s trail information to plan the Adirondack Trail or Inspiration Trail, and include the Patterson Monument or Stone Tower on the route.
cards.short_summary: A MetroPark with short trails, Adirondack-style shelters, Dogwood Pond, and historic points of interest.
cards.evidence_claim: Five Rivers MetroParks lists the 1.46-mile Adirondack Trail, 0.4-mile Inspiration Trail, Patterson Monument, Stone Tower, shelters, and Dogwood Pond at Hills & Dales MetroPark.
cards.access_notes: Check Five Rivers MetroParks alerts and trail information before setting out.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Kettering College ceremonies and recurring campus gatherings centered on healthcare, service, and faith.

cards.title: Start the year at Convocation
cards.subtitle: Academic-year opening ceremony
cards.notes: Watch for the fall Convocation announcement and join the faculty, staff, and students as the college formally opens the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing Kettering College opening-of-year ceremony with academic regalia and a faculty processional.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College describes Convocation as a long-standing tradition that formally symbolizes the beginning of the school year.
cards.source_title: Convocation Ceremony Returns to Campus | Kettering College
cards.access_notes: Check Kettering College event communications for the current ceremony details.

cards.title: Attend the Nursing Dedication
cards.subtitle: First-year Nursing milestone
cards.notes: If you are a first-year Nursing student, follow program communications for this dedication ceremony and its profession-of-service focus.
cards.short_summary: A time-honored first-year Nursing ceremony marking entry into the profession.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College calls its Nursing Dedication ceremony a time-honored tradition for first-year Nursing students.
cards.source_title: Kettering College Holds Nursing Dedication Ceremony | Kettering College
cards.access_notes: For first-year Nursing students; confirm current participation details with the program.

cards.title: Recite the Florence Nightingale Pledge
cards.subtitle: Nursing Dedication Ceremony
cards.notes: At the Nursing Dedication, listen for the pledge and join only when included as part of your program’s ceremony instructions.
cards.short_summary: Nursing students stand together to devote themselves to the profession during the dedication ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: At Kettering College’s Nursing Dedication ceremony, students devote themselves to nursing by saying the Florence Nightingale Pledge.
cards.source_title: Kettering College Holds Nursing Dedication Ceremony | Kettering College
cards.access_notes: Part of the Nursing Dedication ceremony for participating first-year Nursing students.

cards.title: Receive the dedication lamp
cards.subtitle: Nursing Dedication Ceremony
cards.notes: Participating Nursing students can look for program guidance on the lamp presentation, which marks the beginning of the nursing journey.
cards.short_summary: Each student receives a lamp as part of Kettering College’s Nursing Dedication ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College reports that each student receives a lamp during the Nursing Dedication ceremony to signify the beginning of the journey.
cards.source_title: Kettering College Holds Nursing Dedication Ceremony | Kettering College
cards.access_notes: For participants in the Nursing Dedication ceremony; verify details with the Nursing program.

cards.title: Mark a program milestone in white
cards.subtitle: Program dedication ceremony
cards.notes: Check your program calendar for White Coat ceremony details and attend as a participant or invited supporter when your cohort is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: One of the recurring program ceremonies Kettering College documents for annual campus photography.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College lists White Coat ceremonies among the campus events it photographs every year.
cards.access_notes: Availability and eligible programs vary; consult your department for the current schedule.

cards.title: Celebrate at the Pinning Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Program dedication ceremony
cards.notes: Follow your department’s graduation and ceremony guidance for the Pinning Ceremony, then attend according to the cohort’s instructions.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Kettering College program ceremony recognized in the college’s annual photography coverage.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College lists Pinning Ceremonies among the program dedications and ceremonies it photographs every year.
cards.access_notes: Confirm which programs and cohorts hold a Pinning Ceremony with the relevant department.

cards.title: Join the Spring into Health 5K
cards.subtitle: Annual photographed campus event
cards.notes: Look for the college’s Spring into Health 5K announcement, then follow the published registration, route, and participation instructions.
cards.short_summary: A named Kettering College event included in the college’s yearly photography coverage.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College lists the Spring into Health 5K among campus events it photographs every year.
cards.access_notes: Check current event communications for date, registration, route, and any participation requirements.

cards.title: Take part in Student Appreciation Week
cards.subtitle: Recurring campus recognition week
cards.notes: Watch student communications for Student Appreciation Week programming and choose the announced activities that fit your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A named recurring Kettering College event recognized in its annual photography planning.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College lists Student Appreciation Week among campus events it photographs every year.
cards.access_notes: Consult current student announcements for dates, locations, and participation details.

cards.title: Gather for Collective
cards.subtitle: Friday-night Campus Ministries gathering
cards.notes: When school is in session, check the chaplain’s weekly email for Collective’s location and arrive for snacks, worship, and fellowship.
cards.short_summary: A weekly Friday-evening Kettering College Campus Ministries gathering with food, worship, and fellowship.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College says Collective meets on Friday evenings during the school term for snacks, worship, and fellowship.
cards.access_notes: Held Friday evenings when school is in session; the weekly chaplain email provides the location.

cards.title: Begin with Welcome Week
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation week
cards.notes: Use the current Welcome Week schedule to plan required orientation items and optional opportunities to meet classmates, faculty, and staff.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled orientation week introducing new students to Kettering College’s values, culture, and community.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering College’s 2026 Welcome Week is designed to introduce students to the college’s faith-based values, campus culture, and community.
cards.access_notes: Use the current Welcome Week schedule for dates, locations, and required-attendee information.
